content.text:
All 18 playbook rules have been reviewed and submitted. Summary:

**Deviations (redlined) — 6, plus 1 missing clause**

| Rule | Section | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| EXCLUSIVITY | 2.2 | Vendor as sole/exclusive provider for the full term, no performance exit — deleted (contradicts 2.1 and 12.3). |
| MFN | 7.2 | Open-ended MFN running against us (best terms given any technology supplier) — deleted. |
| LD | 7.6 | USD 25,000/day liquidated damages on us for any dependency delay, uncapped — deleted. |
| RENEWAL | 8.2 | 180-day non-renewal notice window (beyond even walk-away) — shortened to 30 days; CPI/3% uplift cap in 8.3 is favourable and untouched. |
| NOSOLICIT | 12.4 | One-way, 18-month, all-personnel no-hire with no advertising carve-out — narrowed to mutual 12-month solicitation-only restriction on involved personnel with carve-outs. |
| AUDIT | 22.1 | Unannounced, unlimited audits with remote system access — limited to once/12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access (aligns with 22.2). |
| T4C | § 9 (missing) | Three-year term with no convenience right — inserted new 9.6: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no Vendor convenience right. |

**Compliant — 11:** LOL-CAP (mutual greater-of 12 months' Fees/USD 1M with full Excluded Claims and uncapped payment obligation), INDEMN (Vendor IP plus misconduct/data/law indemnities; our indemnity stays narrow), NONCOMPETE (12.3 preserves our freedom), GOVLAW (New York law and New York County courts), ASSIGN (free affiliate/successor assignment; no Vendor right on our change of control), IP (we own Data and Deliverables with assignment; perpetual licence back), LICENSE (affiliates/contractors, perpetual paid-up, revocation only for uncured breach), WARRANTY (90-day Deliverable/term-long hosted conformance with non-exclusive remedies), INSURANCE (all limits met), MINCOMMIT (no minimums), TRANSITION (6 months' assistance, 30-day data return, certified deletion).

Note on internal conflicts: Sections 2.2, 7.2, 12.4 and 22.1 each contradict the customer-protective language elsewhere in the document (2.1, 12.3, 22.2), which supports our position that these four are anomalous inserts rather than negotiated terms.
